newsitem.title: FINLAND: DATA, CELLNET INVESTMENT FOCUS -HELSINGIN PUHELIN.
newsitem.headline: DATA, CELLNET INVESTMENT FOCUS -HELSINGIN PUHELIN.

text.p: Finnish local telephone operator Helsingin Puhelin's investment focus is on data communications, mobile phone networks and on corporate wideband infrastructure, CEO Matti Mattheiszen said on Monday.

He said the company is investing some 700 million markka per year and will need the money raised from its planned issue of seven million new E shares. The issue price for the five markka nominal value shares will be published on August 29.

"We will focus on mobile networks, data communications networks and some corporate wideband networks ... and those are the sectors which show the most in the profit and loss account," Mattheiszen told a news conference.

The company is now owned fully by cooperative Helsingin Puhelinyhdistys (HPY) which will retain 85 percent of shares and 96 percent of votes after the offering of shares to cooperative members, who get free rights to subscribe 10 new shares per membership certificate.
The company plans to seek a listing after the share issue.

Cooperative certificates have given discounts on base fees and members would continue to enjoy that benefit even after using or selling their share subscription rights, but phone calls had been and would remain market-price-based, Mattheiszen said.
Helsingin Puhelin chairman Kurt Nordman told the news conference that HPY would begin this autumn to review its long-term role as main owner of the company.

"We will consider whether to give members a chance to convert membership certificates for HPY's remaining E shares ... and how to carry out its role as main owner while promoting the benefits of its members," he said.
He also said that it would be possible for HPY to convert vote-strong K shares which give no right to dividends into E shares which carry only one vote each.
HPY owns 32.32 million K shares and eight million E shares. Each K share carries five votes.
Mattheiszen said Helsingin Puhelin would later define its dividend policy but that the company aimed to "distribute a significant portion of profits".
